tells: It has a coherent, highly finished house illustration system: flat vector with rim highlights, soft inner glows and consistent character construction. This is mature studio explainer work.

Every frame is a different set-up (villain control room, stylised heat-map title, bird characters at a card table, a mammoth in snow). The narrative choreography moves through metaphors instead of repeating one layout.
It has a bold, saturated palette with a clear temperature logic: warm and cold maps, a violet mammoth against pale ice.

tells: It is hand-painted frame by frame with visible bristle drag and dry-brush edges. The texture is clearly physical or carefully emulated, not a default vector.
The Chrysler spire breaks down into abstract stripes, lattices and grids, suggesting real transformation choreography between frames: city → pattern → abstraction.
The palette is limited and deliberate (cobalt, green, white, yellow, red, black), with a Mondrian and Broadway Boogie-Woogie nod that fits the New York subject.
There is no type visible. The absence works, because the piece is a purely painterly visual essay.
gaps: The middle frames (plain stripes, crossed lines) are thin as stand-alone images. They need more density and layering between the iconic opener and the busy finale.
The art-history reference is fairly direct. Pushing it toward a more personal reading of the city would make it more memorable.
Finish and consistency vary (changing aspect ratios, sparse versus dense frames). D's every-frame-a-poster discipline is the bar.

tells: It builds a specific world of circus and fortune-telling iconography: tiger, tarot cards with a horseshoe, cannon, a strongman barbell held by gloved hands. The motifs are coherent and evocative.
The palette is distinctive and unusual (deep lacquer red, teal-grey foliage, ochre, cream). It is rich without going garish.
The material is real: woven or canvas print texture, halftone grain, risograph-like shading and soft cast shadows. It feels like printed ephemera brought to life.
The botanical border has hidden eyes in the leaves, which rewards a second look. Each frame works as a poster on its own.
Hero objects change while the decorative field shifts and regrows, implying choreographed transitions instead of static swaps.
No type is visible. Its absence suits the piece, because the iconography carries it like a wordless title sequence.
gaps: The hero objects always sit centred and similarly scaled. Varying framing and depth (close-ups, overlaps, motion across frame) would add surprise.
The background pattern changes only a little between frames. A stronger progression or turn in the world would deepen the narrative.
If this is a title or brand piece, introducing type crafted in the same printed-ephemera language would complete the system.

defects: Shots hold almost dead still: in all three pairs (1/6 s apart) only a faint caustic shimmer changes on the lemon and the tea surface, and the bag does not move at all
The opening cup frame leaves the lower ~45% of the frame empty brown: no word appears there yet, so the frame reads as unfinished rather than as negative space
The pack hold at the end (frames 5 and 6 match apart from the 'Out Friday.' line) is about 3.7 s of near-static picture
Swirl in the first cup is a flat 2D distortion with a dot at the centre and a smeared window reflection. It reads as a procedural filter, not liquid

The topographic contour lines at 100% have stair-stepped, uneven-width edges and look like a marching-squares threshold with light aliasing. They also cross behind the 'Ethiopia' italic and compete with it
The lemon segment texture is a repeated stretched-dash pattern with radial seams that look drawn on. It reads as CG, not fruit
The kraft bag is a flat vector with a hand-drawn shadow. It has no folds, gusset or label curvature, so it reads as a template mockup
Audio noise bursts are brick-walled at about 20 kHz with flat rectangular envelopes. Together with static harmonic stacks, this is the signature of synthesized placeholder whooshes
gaps: Motion is mostly hard swaps between static posters. The pour, the transformation from flavour note to cup, and the reveal of the bag are never animated with weight, overlap or follow-through. A top studio would make liquid, fruit and pack physically turn into one another, and here nothing moves enough to carry the 'pour' idea

There is no energy arc: change spikes are scattered across seconds 3–11 and then the piece flatlines on a long static pack hold. The ending doesn't rhyme with the opening cup (for example, a cup poured from the bag) and doesn't land a final beat

The sound is thin and generated: plucked harmonic tones with stepped decays plus identical band-limited white-noise swooshes. It has no real foley (pour, ceramic, paper rustle), no low-end bed and no build. Hits roughly track the cuts, but the arrangement is a repeated loop of tick-whoosh with no dynamic shape
